cards.explanation: The answer is none at all. David says they “…attack me without cause.” He gives them no reason because, as he tells it, there isn't one. That's like getting an angry one-star review from someone who never even walked into the bakery. Friends, that stings.

The answer is a man of prayer. David says, “…but I am a man of prayer.” People are accusing him, and that's how he describes himself. I think that's a strong thing to be known for, because my own comebacks always come out soggy.

The answer is an accuser. The prayer says, “let an accuser stand at his right hand.” That's the very spot where you'd hope for a helper, and the prayer puts an accuser there instead. Hang onto that picture, friends. This psalm brings the same spot back at the end.

The answer is guilty. The prayer says, “When he is tried, let him be found guilty, and may his prayer be regarded as sin.” Those are both requests, and one of them is about his prayer. I think this part is heavy, and it's okay to sit with that for a second.

The answer is True. Verse 11 says, “May the creditor seize all he owns, and strangers plunder the fruits of his labor.” The prayer goes from his family to his belongings. I think that's a hard verse to read.

The answer is False. Verse 12 says, “May there be no one to extend kindness to him, and no one to favor his fatherless children.” The prayer asks that no one favor them, not that someone would. It's a heavy verse, and I think it hurts to read.

The answer is show. Verse 16 says, “For he never thought to show kindness…” The prayer gives its reason right there, and it's about kindness that never crossed his mind to show. It's about showing kindness, not receiving it.

The answer is that cursing would fall on him and blessing would stay far away. Verse 17 says, “The cursing that he loved, may it fall on him; the blessing in which he refused to delight, may it be far from him.” The prayer asks that the cursing he loved fall on him, and that the blessing he refused be far from him. That request lines up with what the man chose.

The answer is True. Verse 19 says, “May it be like a robe wrapped about him, like a belt tied forever around him.” The cursing is pictured as a belt tied on for good. A belt I understand. I've got an apron string in a bow behind my back, and I still can't reach it.

The answer is his accusers who speak evil against him. Verse 20 says, “May this be the LORD’s reward to my accusers, to those who speak evil against me.” David hands the whole matter to the LORD. He asks for the LORD's reward, not his own. That's the same group from the start of the psalm, the ones with the lying tongues.

The answer is that he is poor and needy. David says, “For I am poor and needy; my heart is wounded within me.” He doesn't bring a résumé. He brings his need. I think that's the best way to walk up to God, with empty hands.

The answer is True. David says, “I am an object of scorn to my accusers; when they see me, they shake their heads.” He describes himself as fading away, and he also describes the scorn and the head shaking. That's a rough thing to go through, friends. I think it hurts.

The answer is that the LORD has done it. David asks, “Let them know that this is Your hand, that You, O LORD, have done it.” He wants the credit to land on the LORD. He's not asking for a victory lap of his own.
The answer is bless. David says, “Though they curse, You will bless.” They bring cursing, and he trusts God to bring blessing. I love how short and sure that line is.

The answer is robe. David prays, “may they wear their shame like a robe.” A robe showed up earlier too, when the cursing was pictured as a robe wrapped about that man (Psalm 109:19). So that clothing picture comes back around.

The answer is False. David says, “With my mouth I will thank the LORD profusely; I will praise Him in the presence of many.” He promises to thank the LORD with his mouth. And he says it will be in the presence of many.

The answer is the LORD. David says, “For He stands at the right hand of the needy one…” Earlier the prayer put an accuser at that spot. Now the LORD is standing there. Friends, that's some switcheroo.
